Set a population to a specified depletion level.

Source: R/om.R
deplete.Rd

Builds an FLBRP object from first-year biological inputs and the supplied catch selectivity, parameterizes it with the FLBiol Beverton-Holt stock-recruitment relationship, and finds the fishing mortality producing the requested fraction of virgin biomass. The resulting equilibrium numbers-at-age replace the first-year abundance in biol; calculated reference points are retained as its "refpts" attribute.

deplete(biol, sel, dep, minfbar = dims(biol)$min, maxfbar = dims(biol)$max)

Arguments

biol

An initialized FLBiol whose first year supplies biological inputs and a Beverton-Holt stock-recruitment relationship.

sel

Catch selectivity at age. Only its first year is used.

dep

Target depletion as a proportion of virgin biomass, between zero and one. Values are applied by iteration.

minfbar

Youngest age included in the fishing-mortality average. Defaults to the minimum age in biol.

maxfbar

Oldest age included in the fishing-mortality average. Defaults to the maximum age in biol and is capped at that age.

Value

biol, with first-year n at the equilibrium depletion level and an attached "refpts" attribute containing the FLBRP reference points.

Details

dep is interpreted as a fraction of virgin total biomass, so 0 denotes the lowest biomass reachable by the reference-point calculation and 1 denotes the unfished biomass. For depletion calculations, multiple fisheries should first be represented by a combined catch selectivity.

Examples

data(ple4.biol)
